answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use a slow-drip reputation lagoon: every new identity starts with a tiny earnings cap and a unique cipher key bound to one verified device. To raise the cap it must complete useful work that peers audit; each finished job adds one verse to its public record, like stanzas of a sonnet, and only a full, consistent sonnet unlocks higher limits. Spinning up a thousand fake identities means solving a thousand cipher challenges and doing a thousand audited jobs, so the attacker pays real compute and time per copy while honest agents climb once and stay.
